newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL blue chips close at year high, 2nd board falls.
newsitem.headline: KL blue chips close at year high, 2nd board falls.

text.p: Malaysian blue-chip stocks surged to a new closing high for 1996, as both local and foreign funds actively bought large-capitalised stocks, while small-cap stocks continued to be sold off by retail punters.
"There has been an improvement in confidence, aided by psychological factors," said Fiona Leong, head of research at JM Sassoon.
The Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks closed up 12.24 points or 1.02 percent to 1,217.96, while the Second Board index closed down 12.15 to 610.74, a 1.95 percent drop.
Volume was higher at 382 million shares.
"There has been quite a lot of institutional interest, but there has been no theme," said Patrick Tan, senior analyst at brokers HG Asia in Kuala Lumpur.

"When the Second Board started to come down, the main board became quite firm, which lent confidence to the market. There has been a combination of factors at work, but why they have all converged today, I'm not too sure," said Tan.

Tenaga was up 20 cents to 11.50, and Sime Darby was up 50 to 9.50. Both stocks contribute significantly to the weightage of the Composite Index. "At these levels on Tenaga it is a bit difficult to call an outright buy on the stock," said Leong.
